latest_release.body:
RIOT-2026.10 "GameOverBugs" - Release Notes
===========================================
RIOT is a multi-threading operating system which enables soft real-time
capabilities and comes with support for a range of devices that are typically
found in the Internet of Things: 8-bit and 16-bit microcontrollers as well as
light-weight 32-bit processors.

RIOT is based on the following design principles: energy-efficiency, soft
real-time capabilities, small memory footprint, modularity, and uniform API
access, independent of the underlying hardware (with partial POSIX compliance).

RIOT is developed by an international open-source community which is
independent of specific vendors (e.g. similarly to the Linux community) and is
licensed with a non-viral copyleft license (LGPLv2.1), which allows indirect
business models around the free open-source software platform provided by RIOT.


About this release
==================

The 2026.10 release includes:

- Improved CoAP support with basic server (#21582) and client (#22266)
  functionality of unicoap, the integration of the libCoAP library (#19889)
  and the removal of unsafe and deprecated nanocoap APIs (#22505, #22861).
  If you need to communicate with legacy non-CoAP endpoints out there, we've
  also got you covered with the newly added integration of picohttpparser
  (#22725).

- We've got a new way of interacting with your favorite RIOT board: Jelly has
  landed (#22634), offering a feature-rich shell interface with autocompletion
  while reducing the binary size of your RIOT application.

- Our 802.15.4 Radio HAL and (Sub)MAC implementation have received major
  improvements (#21578, #21973, #22784, #22777) and support for two additional
  radios: The AT86RF2XX family (#21674) as well as the KW41ZRF radio (#21992).

- Three new boards have been added: STM32 Nucleo-G491RE (#22458), Seeed Studio
  Xiao ESP32C6 (#22400) and the ZedBoard (#22548, our first board with
  RISCV64!); while two boards have been deprecated: TelosB and Zolertia Z1
  (#22716). We also got support for the mGBA emulator of the Game Boy Advanced
  (#22776), which facilitated several improvements on this little fun device
  (#22776, #22908).

- The Docker container used for BUILD_IN_DOCKER=1 got a version update to
  Ubuntu 26.04 Resolute Raccoon 🦝 (#22692) and the build system got many
  smaller and larger optimizations to reduce the build time (#22898, #22355,
  #22780, #22733, #22672, #22669, #22837, #22851 and more).

- Our test infrastructure for CI, daily, weekly and release tests got cleaned-up
  and hardened (#22787, #22653, #22954, #22671, #22956, #22960, #22942, #22958,
  #22951 and more)

411 pull requests, composed of 792 commits, have been merged since the
last release, and 29 issues have been solved. 49 people contributed with
code in 70 days. 3025 files have been touched with 107371 (+) insertions and
38492 deletions (-).


Notations used below
====================

    + means new feature/item
    * means modified feature/item
    - means removed feature/item


New features and changes
========================

Core
----

* byteorder.h: remove unused union members (#22622)


System Libraries
----------------

+ sys/base64: add ACCESS() attribute (#22369)
+ sys/fmt: add scn_bool() helper function (#22503)
+ sys/isrpipe: add isrpipe_get_free() (#22934)
+ sys/jelly: Add basic support for the Jelly tool (#22634)
* rust: Update riot-sys and -wrappers (#22683)
* sys/base64: minor improvements and documentation updates (#22383)
* sys/can: annotate functions with ACCESS() (#22382)
* sys/cpp_new_delete: handle allocation failures (#22418)
* sys/hashes: minor improvements (#22386)
* sys/include: Macro for ANSI Colours and Text Styles (#22621)
* sys/isrpipe: fix isrpipe_write() return value documentation (#22453)
* sys/shell/ifconfig: Give helpful error message when missing IPv6
  support (#22689)
* sys/shell: Initial bplib shell command (#22674)
* sys/walltime: improve documentation (#22630)
